$comment: The repository settings this project has DECIDED, so a scheduled job can read the live values
back and say so when they drift. See docs/decisions/0004-admin-settings-must-be-read-back.md.
Repo settings, protection, rulesets — and now the github-pages ENVIRONMENT, which was the one
that actually refused a release (see 0013). DNS is still the only thing read back by hand,
because it lives at Cloudflare and no GitHub token can see it.

private.why: Public repo. Flipping it would break Pages and every link.

default_branch.why: Every workflow, protection rule and required check names it.

has_issues.why: The weekly hotspots report opens and edits one rolling issue; disabled, it fails.

allow_auto_merge.why: The branch -> PR -> auto-merge lifecycle depends on it.

delete_branch_on_merge.why: Merged branches accumulate otherwise, and stale ones get re-used by mistake.

allow_squash_merge.why: Produces one revertable commit per PR, which is most of what 0001 asks for.

allow_merge_commit.why: Also produces a single revertable unit.

allow_rebase_merge.why: The one merge method that does NOT: N commits on main with nothing tying them together, so there is no single thing to revert. Disabled 2026-08-03.

required_status_checks.why: The JOB KEY in tests.yml, not the workflow name. A required context that never reports blocks every PR forever.

strict.why: TURNED OFF 2026-08-07, deliberately. The argument FOR it is real and is kept here rather than deleted: a branch that is not up to date passed `test` against a tree nobody is merging. What outweighed it is that nine PRs landed in one session, and this rule makes merging strictly serial — rebase, wait for CI, merge, repeat — which at eight minutes a run is most of a day. The guard that replaces it is that main is re-checked after a batch lands, and that every branch is proved locally before it is pushed. Reopen it the moment merges stop coming in batches.

requires_pull_request.why: Step 7. Ends the scaffold's deliberate direct-to-main suspension.

enforce_admins.why: ⚠️ THE ONE THAT WAS DECORATIVE. With this false, the only person who can push is exempt from every rule above — verified 2026-08-03 by a probe push that reported 'Bypassed rule violations' and succeeded. Protection that cannot stop the sole developer stops nobody.

allow_force_pushes.why: History on main is not rewritten. See 0006.

allow_deletions.why: main is named by every workflow and protection rule.

$comment: THE SETTING THAT REFUSED THE FIRST RELEASE. `v0.1.0` built green and the deploy was rejected,
because enabling Pages from a branch had seeded this environment with a `main` branch rule and
a tag matches no branch rule. Word for word the predecessor's v1.4.0 incident. See 0013.
Read with SETTINGS_READ_TOKEN. If the report says NOT CHECKED for these, the fine-grained PAT
needs *Environments: read* — a separate permission from *Administration: read*.

policies.why: EXACTLY ONE, and a tag. A release is a tag; nothing else may reach the origin players installed from. A `main` branch rule here is not an extra permission, it is a second definition of what a release is — and while one exists, any branch deployment publishes staging to every installed app. Deleted rather than left alongside (0013).

$comment: A SECOND system stating overlapping policy. Rulesets and classic branch protection both
apply and the most restrictive wins, so a change here is invisible to a check that reads
only the protection endpoint — the same blind spot this file was extended to close, in a
different API. Covered rather than consolidated, because consolidating means moving the
required `test` context across and removing classic protection, which is a decision.

main.why: Blocks deletion and force-push on the default branch and requires a PR, with nobody bypassing.

allowed_merge_methods.why: ⚠️ MUST AGREE WITH allow_rebase_merge ABOVE. A rebase merge lands N commits on main with nothing tying them together, so there is no single thing to revert (0001). Listing it here would leave the ruleset silently permitting what the repo flag forbids, and the repo flag is one click from being flipped back.

required_approving_review_count.why: A sole developer cannot approve their own PR; requiring one would block every merge.
